title: Device makers license third-party frontier models for assistants by H1 2027
body: Apple's WWDC decision to power the rebuilt Siri with a custom ~1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model, on a multi-year deal reported around $1 billion a year rather than ship its own model, is the clearest signal yet that even the most vertically integrated device maker has concluded that owning the device base and the user gateway beats owning the best model. That reframes the assistant race as a build-vs-buy decision: the frontier-training treadmill (capex, scarce researchers, the cost of falling a generation behind) is brutal for anyone whose core business is hardware or an OS, while the durable moat is the install base and the default-assistant slot that sits in front of it. Expect this to harden into the explicit default pattern - license the brain, own the gateway - across the consumer-assistant tier. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by H1 2027 at least one other major consumer-device, OS, or platform vendor whose flagship assistant is currently first-party - the strongest candidates being Samsung (Galaxy/Bixby), Amazon (Alexa), or a major automaker's in-car assistant - formally announces that its built-in assistant is powered by a licensed third-party frontier model (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, or a comparable lab) rather than a wholly in-house model, with a named lab partner and a shipping or beta build. Apple's privacy-by-topology framing - a small on-device model plus stateless server inference with PII stripped before anything reaches the licensed model - also supplies the template that makes such a deal defensible to a privacy-conscious base, lowering the bar for the next vendor to follow.

reasoning.because: Apple licensed a custom ~1.2T-param Gemini (~$1B/yr) to power rebuilt Siri instead of its own model
reasoning.given: frontier training is too costly/risky for device makers; the moat is install base + assistant slot
reasoning.so_that: another major consumer-device/OS/platform vendor licenses a third-party frontier model for its built-in assistant
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027, a named-lab assistant deal from Samsung, Amazon, or an automaker
reasoning.plain_language: Phone and gadget makers will rent a top AI brain from someone else instead of building their own, like Apple just did.

summary: Apple ran the rebuilt Siri on a licensed Google Gemini model, not its own, signaling device makers value the install base and assistant gateway over the model itself. By H1 2027 expect another major vendor - Samsung, Amazon, or an automaker - to license a third-party model for its assistant.
